# Contributing

Thanks for helping. Fixes, test cases and better error messages are always welcome. Open an issue before starting anything large, such as a new format or engine, because rebake is deliberately narrow.

## Rules that don't bend

These come from [the spec](../docs/SPEC.md), and a change that breaks one won't be merged:

- **Nothing leaves the tab.** No uploads, no third-party origins, no analytics, no cookies, no server-side fallback.
- **Only offer what works here, and fail loudly.** Never return a file in a format other than the one asked for.
- **No framework, and a shell under 50 KB.** Conversion code loads on demand, in a worker.
- **The first screen is the tool.** No pitch copy. See [DESIGN.md](../docs/DESIGN.md).

## Set up

You need Node 22 (`.nvmrc` has it), and for the tests ffmpeg, pandoc and qpdf. HEIC fixtures need macOS, and tests that need them skip themselves elsewhere.

```sh
npm ci
npx playwright install
npm run fixtures      # writes to ../rebake-fixtures, or $REBAKE_FIXTURES
```

## Check your change

```sh
npm run build         # checks vendor/, types everything, then builds dist/
npm run test:quick    # Chromium
npm test              # all browsers
```

`tests/media.spec.ts` and `tests/hdr.spec.ts` need Safari's real codecs, so on Linux they skip WebKit, and CI runs them on macOS. A local `chrome` project runs where Google Chrome is installed, because Playwright's Chromium has no HEVC. The memory tests are opt-in:

```sh
npm run fixtures:large
REBAKE_LARGE=1 npx playwright test tests/large.spec.ts --workers=1
```

Known browser gaps are listed, with reasons, in `tests/lib/media-gaps.ts`. A listed gap that stops being one fails the suite. To check a deployed site, run `REBAKE_URL=https://rebake.app npx playwright test`.

## Things that will catch you out

- **Tests run `dist/`.** `npm run build` stops at a type error, tests included, and Playwright then tests the old build. If a failure makes no sense, check that the build printed "built in".
- **Port 4319.** Playwright won't reuse a server, so stop any stray `npm run serve` first.
- **`vite dev` sends no CSP.** Anything touching engines has to be tried in `npm run build && npm run serve`, where `public/_headers` applies. The CSP forbids `eval`, `new Function` and inline styles, so set styles through `element.style`.
- **The first `npm run dev` conversion in each engine can abort.** Vite reloads the page when it finds a new dependency. Try again once it settles.
- **Never edit `vendor/`.** It's generated by `npm run vendor` and checked against `vendor/SHA256SUMS` on every build. After bumping an engine's package, run `npm run vendor`.
- **Motion has no late corrections.** Conditional UI goes through `reveal()` and `reshape()` in `src/ui/motion.ts`. `tests/polish.spec.ts` samples frames, because a screenshot can't see a snap.
- **Codec checks lie.** `isConfigSupported` says yes to encoders that write broken streams, so rebake runs a real encode. Treat a failure as unsupported, never a slow answer. See "Capabilities" in [ARCHITECTURE.md](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

## Adding a format or engine

[ARCHITECTURE.md](../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) has the steps. Before any code, try the library in a built app under the real CSP. GPL and LGPL code ships only as separate, replaceable files, and every dependency goes in [THIRD_PARTY.md](../docs/THIRD_PARTY.md).

## Pull requests

- Keep each one to one change, with a test that fails without it.
- Write commit subjects in the imperative, like `Skip the GIF motion test where Linux WebKit can't offer GIF`.
- Match the code around you. Comments say why, not what. `.editorconfig` covers whitespace.
- UI text is plain English with no codec jargon on the common path.

## Reporting bugs

Use the issue form, and never attach a private file. A description of the formats and the exact message is usually enough, or make a small file that shows the same problem.
